note: Target admits a direct finite counting proof. Count length-(2k+1) words with an H-majority. Partition by j, the number of T letters before the (k+1)-st H: the prefix has k H and j T in binom(k+j,j) arrangements, the distinguished next letter is H, and k-j suffix positions are arbitrary, giving 2^(k-j)binom(k+j,j). Letter complementation shows exactly half of all 2^(2k+1) words have H-majority, hence 4^k. Endpoint k=0 works.
